Rafael / Monica / Jordan — thanks for the thread. I reviewed ACME's redlines and our draft response. Summary of proposed positions below (feel free to lift into the DPA redline):

1) Roles and Definitions
- Proposed text: "Customer is the controller of Customer Data; Redwood Inference is a processor that processes Customer Data on Customer's behalf. Redwood does not act as a controller for Customer Data processed solely to provide the Service."
- Rationale: keeps model-development exceptions separate (we'll note below).

2) Logs and Telemetry
- Proposed text: "Redwood collects operational logs and telemetry necessary to provide and secure the Service. Operational logs may include timestamps, request metadata, model/route identifiers, and anonymized usage metrics. Redwood will not retain request payloads or any full-text customer inputs in logs beyond 30 days except as required for security investigations or by law. Customers may request extended retention or deletion of logs via support ticket."
- Rationale: 30-day default retention balances debugging/ops needs with customer privacy. If ACME needs different retention, we can offer contract language or a Dedicated/Private option.

3) Embeddings and Use of Derived Data
- Proposed text: "Embeddings or other derived artifacts generated from Customer Data are treated as Customer Data. Redwood will not use Customer Data or derived embeddings to train models or improve model weights except with explicit Customer consent. Aggregated, de-identified telemetry may be used for service quality improvements."
- Rationale: protects ACME's intellectual property and PII concerns while allowing aggregated product improvements.

4) Subprocessors and Notification
- Proposed text: "Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors at https://drive.redwood.ai/subprocessors and will provide at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor. Customer may object in writing within the notice period. If objection is reasonable, the parties will negotiate in good faith; if unresolved, Customer may terminate certain Processing activities."

5) International Transfers
- Proposed text: "Redwood will rely on EU SCCs (as updated) and other lawful transfer mechanisms; documentation can be provided upon request. For UK and other jurisdictions, equivalent mechanisms will be used."

If ACME accepts these, I can produce a clean redline and we can generate a DocuSign envelope. Monica: confirm we can operationalize the 30-day log retention and the subprocessors public link. Rafael: once confirmed I'll prepare the final DPA for signature.
